title: Latency/$ Benchmark — Results QC Notes (Outliers, Reruns, Infra Noise, Sign-off)
content:
Doc purpose
- This doc captures QA/QC notes for the public-facing Latency/$ benchmark dataset.
- Audience: Perf/Evals + SRE + Marketing reviewers who need to validate the results are (a) internally consistent, (b) explainable, and (c) safe to publish.
- Scope: Chat + embeddings baseline workloads; regional runs (NA/EU/APAC) using the benchmark-lab harness.
- Non-goals: publishing raw request logs or customer traces (explicitly out of scope).

Owners / accountability
- Methodology + QC lead: Claire Dubois
- Execution / reruns: Rina Kobayashi
- Variance + confidence language: Sana Farid
- Latency trace sanity checks: Caleb Johnson
- Cost attribution + metering validation: Nadia Rahman
- SRE capacity window + infra notes: Sean Gallagher
- Methodology sponsor (final sign-off): Jonas Weber

Dataset inputs & build identifiers
- Source table: shared_drives/engineering/applied-ml/benchmark-results-raw-table.json
- Export pipeline: benchmark-lab public table generator (see github:benchmark-lab/pr-159-export-csv-and-public-table-generator)
- Run window (primary): 2025-01-30 → 2025-02-06 (local time per region; exact timestamps stored in artifacts bucket)
- Harness version: benchmark-lab @ commit noted in run artifacts (post PR-153 merge)
- Runtime flags: using the benchmark-consistency config (see github:redwood/pr-18421-runtime-config-for-benchmark-consistency)

High-level QC summary (what changed since first pass)
- Reruns performed for 3 region/model combinations due to p95 variance threshold breaches and/or suspected infra noise.
- One cost-metering anomaly corrected (unit conversion in a single region’s cost snapshot; see “Cost attribution checks”).
- One APAC run discarded due to transient elevated network RTT affecting streaming token timing; re-collected during a clean window.
- Final dataset is internally consistent across:
  - derived metrics (latency/$ matches formula)
  - pricing inputs used during the window
  - token counts (prompt/completion totals align with harness logs)
  - expected ordering (p50 <= p95; throughput > 0; cost > 0)

QC gates (must pass)
1) Completeness
- For each included model x region x workload:
  - >= 5 valid runs (after warmup removal)
  - each run >= minimum sample size threshold (see methodology)
  - no missing key fields: p50, p95, throughput, cost_per_1m_tokens, latency_per_dollar

2) Metric consistency
- Validate: latency_per_dollar = (tokens_per_second) / (dollars_per_second)
  - dollars_per_second derived from cost_per_1m_tokens and measured token throughput
  - cross-check computed latency/$ against benchmark-lab output for 20 random rows + all rerun rows
- Validate units:
  - latency in ms (p50/p95)
  - throughput in tokens/sec
  - cost_per_1m_tokens in USD
  - latency/$ in (ms per USD) is NOT used; we report “tokens/sec per $/sec” via the derived ratio. Marketing label remains “Latency/$” but explanations clarify the computation.

3) Distribution sanity
- p95/p50 ratio within expected envelope by workload (chat has larger tail than embeddings).
- Streaming vs non-streaming: ensure we are using consistent definition (TTFT excluded from end-to-end token latency metric per methodology; capture TTFT separately only in internal artifacts).

4) Variance thresholds
- Automatic rerun trigger (per PR-153 policy):
  - if run-to-run p95 differs by > 8% relative std dev OR
  - if latency/$ differs by > 10% relative std dev OR
  - if any single run deviates > 2.5σ from the median without an explained infra event.

5) Infra event correlation
- Any outlier row must have either:
  - corresponding infra note (capacity, GPU saturation, host interrupts, networking) OR
  - explicit “no infra correlation found; rerun performed” record.

6) Claim-safety checks (public benchmarking guidelines)
- No absolute claims without intervals/variance language.
- Region-to-region differences include caveats about network proximity, cross-region routing policies, and time-of-day variability.


Outliers & reruns log (by issue)

A) APAC (primary issue: network jitter affecting token timing)
- Symptom:
  - 2025-02-02 APAC chat workload showed elevated p95 (+18–25% vs other APAC runs) for two models.
  - Throughput remained roughly stable; tail latency worsened, especially in streaming segments.
- Evidence:
  - Elevated client↔edge RTT and intermittent packet loss observed on monitoring screenshots during the same window.
  - Not correlated with GPU saturation (GPU util < expected peak; no memory pressure).
- Decision:
  - Discard the impacted run set.
  - Rerun during the next clean APAC window (2025-02-04).
- Outcome:
  - Post-rerun: p95 back within ±6% of APAC median; latency/$ variance below threshold.

B) EU region (primary issue: host-level noise / partial noisy neighbor)
- Symptom:
  - EU embeddings workload for one model had unusually low throughput (-14%) while p50 latency was not proportionally elevated.
  - This pattern generally indicates batching disruption or host contention rather than model/runtime change.
- Investigation notes:
  - Host metrics indicated higher CPU steal on inference coordinator nodes (not GPU nodes).
  - No runtime deploy during window; container images unchanged.
- Decision:
  - Rerun embeddings suite for that model in EU after rescheduling to a different host pool.
- Outcome:
  - Throughput normalized; cost metrics unchanged; latency/$ improved accordingly.
  - Mark original EU row as invalid (excluded from final export).

C) NA region (primary issue: one-time GPU clock anomaly)
- Symptom:
  - Single run with p95 latency spike (+12%) at similar throughput.
- Investigation notes:
  - GPU clocks temporarily below expected boost; coincided with thermal event flagged in node telemetry.
- Decision:
  - Keep run logs for internal reference; rerun to confirm it was transient.
- Outcome:
  - Rerun normal; original outlier excluded from aggregation.


Infra noise investigation (what we checked)
- Checked release/deploy calendars for runtime and routing changes during run windows.
  - No runtime changes during rerun windows; all runs used the same benchmark configuration.
- Checked SRE capacity windows:
  - All benchmark runs stayed within safety limits; no production SLO regressions were observed.
- Checked GPU saturation and queueing:
  - Confirmed no sustained GPU saturation beyond target envelope (brief spikes acceptable).
  - Confirmed no request queue buildup (queue depth stable) in “clean” runs.
- Checked cross-region routing:
  - Confirmed runs pinned to target region and did not fall back to alternate regions.
  - Verified region headers/selection mechanism consistent with docs (see github:redwood-openai-compat/pr-318-region-header-doc-clarification).


Cost attribution checks (Nadia)
- Goal: ensure cost_per_1m_tokens and derived dollars/sec were computed from the intended price sheet and usage accounting snapshot.
- Checks performed:
  1) Random sample reconciliation (10 rows): recompute cost_per_1m_tokens from pricing inputs + measured token counts; match within rounding.
  2) Region multiplier validation: ensure regional pricing multipliers applied consistently.
  3) Spot-check “embeddings vs chat” pricing mapping (correct SKU mapping).
- Issue found:
  - One region’s cost snapshot had a unit conversion typo in an intermediate sheet used during first-pass aggregation (1K vs 1M normalization). This affected a small subset of derived latency/$ rows.
- Fix:
  - Recompute cost_per_1m_tokens from the canonical pricing source; regenerate derived columns via benchmark-lab exporter.
- Outcome:
  - Corrected rows now align with recomputed values; no further discrepancies found.


Latency/trace data sanity checks (Caleb)
- Verified:
  - p50 <= p95 for all exported rows.
  - No negative or zero latencies.
  - Token counts per request within the configured distribution envelopes.
  - Warmup runs excluded (first N minutes / first M requests per methodology).
- Notable observation:
  - A small number of runs had unusually good TTFT but normal steady-state token latency; this is acceptable and likely reflects cache warming patterns, but TTFT is not used in the public “Latency/$” calculation.


Data hygiene / export rules for public table
- Fields included for public consumption (sanitized): model, model_family, region, workload_type, concurrency_profile, p50_ms, p95_ms, throughput_toks_per_s, cost_per_1m_tokens_usd, latency_per_dollar (derived), run_window_start, run_window_end, notes (high level)
- Fields excluded:
  - hostnames / instance ids
  - internal cluster names
  - per-run raw logs
  - any customer identifiers (none were present by design)


Open questions resolved during QC
- Q: Is “Latency/$” confusing as a label?
  - Resolution: keep label for continuity, but add explicit definition in methodology appendix and landing page FAQ. Also ensure charts/tooltips clarify it’s a derived performance-per-cost metric, not “milliseconds per dollar”.
- Q: Do we publish confidence intervals?
  - Resolution: include variance language and confidence-band visuals where appropriate; do not overfit on precise statistical claims. Use “observed range across repeated runs” framing consistent with public claims guidelines.


Final sign-off checklist (Perf/Evals)
- [x] Methodology adhered to (workloads, distributions, concurrency profiles, warmup rules)
- [x] Rerun policy executed where triggers fired; all reruns documented above
- [x] Known bad runs excluded and marked invalid in source table
- [x] Derived metrics recomputed using deterministic exporter
- [x] Cost attribution verified against canonical pricing inputs
- [x] Region pinning verified; no unintended fallback
- [x] Public export contains no sensitive infrastructure identifiers
- [x] Outlier explanations exist for every excluded row (or rerun confirmed transient)
- [x] Claims language reviewed against Public Benchmarking Claims Guidelines
- [x] “Limitations” section includes infra-noise + regional variability caveats

Approvals
- Claire Dubois (Benchmark methodology & QA lead): Approved — 2025-02-10
- Rina Kobayashi (Execution): Approved — 2025-02-10
- Sana Farid (Variance/statistical review): Approved — 2025-02-10
- Nadia Rahman (Cost/metering validation): Approved — 2025-02-10
- Jonas Weber (Methodology sponsor): Approved — 2025-02-10

Notes for Marketing / Docs
- When highlighting “headline” findings, avoid single-run precision. Use wording like:
  - “Across repeated runs in each region…”
  - “Observed p95 ranges…”
  - “Results are reproducible within the documented variance thresholds…”
- If asked about anomalies:
  - Use the summary above: APAC network jitter rerun; EU host contention rerun; NA thermal clock event rerun.
  - Emphasize that reruns are part of the pre-registered QC policy, not selective cherry-picking.

Appendix: quick reference — rerun triggers used
- p95 variance trigger: > 8% relative std dev across runs
- latency/$ variance trigger: > 10% relative std dev across runs
- single-run outlier trigger: > 2.5σ from median (requires infra correlation or rerun)
